text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementTechnologyWe Attribute Personalities to Chatbots, Even When We Know BetterWe can spot the bot, but we treat it like a person anywayKFBy Kristen French3:00 PM CST on November 6, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleTalk to a chatbot for even a few minutes, and you may begin to feel that someone is in there, a person-shaped thing with a specific temperament. Anthropic’s AI chatbot Claude is like an overly thoughtful colleague, who spends too much time in the library and above all, aims to please. xAI’s Grok is direct, contrarian, anti-woke and on occasion egregiously offensive.This is called the “ELIZA effect,” and it is a term coined many decades ago. In the 1960s, MIT computer scientist Joseph Weizenbaum created the world’s first chatbot, named ELIZA, before “chatbot” was even a word. Weizenbaum noticed that most users quickly anthropomorphized the program, sharing deeply personal secrets with it.  Read more: “AI Already Knows Us Too Well”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
